detail.summary: Observer disagreement in scientific contexts is often driven by subjective epistemological frameworks and cognitive biases rather than mere data scarcity. Framing and interest-driven selection function as filters that create persistent interpretive differences.

detail.title: Journal of Identity and Observer Epistemology
detail.summary: This cycle progresses the research on personal identity construction and observer epistemology. Notebooks for 'Cognitive Foundations of Personal Identity' and 'Epistemological Foundations of Observer Disagreement' have been synthesized using the collected sources, documenting the reconstructive nature of memory and the role of framing in disagreement. A follow-up research action on curious exploration mechanisms is initiated.
